title: Development and Democracy
shortDescription: Concepts of development, human development, India's approach, welfare schemes and sustainable development.
genZNote: Is democracy good for development? India's answer: growth AND rights AND welfare. This chapter links everything to real schemes.

sections.heading: What Development Means
bullets: Economic growth (GDP) vs development (people's well-being); Human Development Index (UNDP): life expectancy, education and per-capita income.
Amartya Sen: "Development as Freedom" — expanding capabilities and freedoms.
Debate: do democracies grow slower or faster? India's experience shows democratic accountability can drive welfare and inclusion.

sections.heading: India's Approach
bullets: Mixed economy and planning (Planning Commission 1950–2014; replaced by NITI Aayog on 1 January 2015); economic reforms of 1991 (LPG).
Welfare/rights legislation: MGNREGA (2005), RTE (2009), NFSA (2013), RTI (2005).
Directive Principles act as the development blueprint; decentralised planning via local bodies.
Sustainable Development Goals (2015, 17 goals by 2030) guide targets; India sits in the "medium human development" group — check the latest HDR.

sections.heading: Tensions and Movements
bullets: Displacement and environment: Narmada Bachao Andolan (Sardar Sarovar on the Narmada, Gujarat) and Chipko highlight development versus livelihood debates.
Inclusive growth: reducing regional and social inequality, empowering women and marginalised groups.
Participatory development: gram sabhas, social audits and cooperatives (Amul model in Gujarat).

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Development in a democracy aims at growth with equity, rights and participation, guided by constitutional values and welfare policies.

commonTraps: Do not equate GDP growth with development.
